section: Satavahana administration, economy, coinage and Prakrit literature (Hala's Gathasaptasati)
subsections: Guilds → craft, interest rates, Indo-Roman ports
Society - metronymics, caste mobility, women donors, debates
Urban administration - Nigama Sabha, towns and Gahapati

accepted.s: Which of the following guilds was associated with oil-pressing during the Satavahana period?
accepted.x: Tilapishaka was the guild of oil-pressers. Kularika was associated with potters, Kolika with weavers and Malakara with florists.
accepted.tq: Use the craft–guild association directly and eliminate neighbouring occupational groups.
accepted.sec: Guilds → craft, interest rates, Indo-Roman ports  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Consider the following pairs:
a. Padhika — Butchers
b. Udayantrika — Water-machines
c. Gandhika — Perfumers
Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
accepted.x: Padhika denoted butchers, Udayantrika or Adyantrika operated water-machines such as ghatiyantras, and Gandhika denoted perfumers; all three pairs are correctly matched.
accepted.tq: Check each occupational term independently before selecting the coded combination.
accepted.sec: Guilds → craft, interest rates, Indo-Roman ports  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following is NOT correctly matched?
accepted.x: Tailika was associated with oil-pressers, not metal workers. Kulara, Malakara and Sarthavaha referred respectively to potters, florists and long-distance or foreign traders.
accepted.tq: Find the one occupational mismatch among closely related guild names.
accepted.sec: Guilds → craft, interest rates, Indo-Roman ports  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The head of a guild in the Satavahana period was generally known as:
accepted.x: A guild was headed by a Sethi or Shreshthi. Sarthavaha referred to a long-distance or foreign trader, while Gahapati was connected with urban administration.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the guild office-holder from urban and trading terms.
accepted.sec: Guilds → craft, interest rates, Indo-Roman ports  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Guilds in the Satavahana period performed which of the following economic functions?
o: They acted as banks and paid interest on deposits.
They issued only royal land grants.
They functioned exclusively as military units.
accepted.x: Guilds acted as banking institutions: they accepted deposits and paid interest, including payments benefiting monasteries.
accepted.tq: Identify the economic function from the institutional role rather than the occupational label.
accepted.sec: Guilds → craft, interest rates, Indo-Roman ports  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The annual rate corresponding to an interest rate of one per cent per month in the Satavahana period was:
accepted.x: One per cent per month amounted to 12 per cent per year. This rate is associated with deposits made with guilds.
accepted.tq: Convert the monthly rate into its annual equivalent.
accepted.sec: Guilds → craft, interest rates, Indo-Roman ports  [APPSC]

accepted.s: In the deposits associated with the Nasik inscription, the rate of three-fourths of one per cent per month was intended for:
o: The purchase of robes for monks
The payment of customs at Bharuch
accepted.x: The deposit carrying interest at three-fourths of one per cent per month was meant for the other needs of monks. The separate one-per-cent monthly deposit provided for monks' robes.
accepted.tq: Separate similar deposits by matching each rate with its stated purpose.
accepted.sec: Guilds → craft, interest rates, Indo-Roman ports  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which Satavahana port was known in Greek accounts as Barygaza?
accepted.x: Bharuch was known as Barygaza. It came under Satavahana control after the defeat of Nahapana.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between the Indian port name and its foreign commercial designation.
accepted.sec: Guilds → craft, interest rates, Indo-Roman ports  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Bharuch came under Satavahana control after the defeat of:
accepted.x: Bharuch or Barygaza came under Satavahana control after Nahapana was defeated. The other rulers belong to different political contexts.
accepted.tq: Use the ruler–event association and avoid substituting another foreign-linked ruler.
accepted.sec: Guilds → craft, interest rates, Indo-Roman ports  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following ports was destroyed by the Sakas, according to the Periplus?
accepted.x: The Periplus records that Kalyan was destroyed by the Sakas. Kantakasela and Maisolia were east-coast ports, while Motupalli belonged to a later Eastern Chalukya context.
accepted.tq: Match the specific event with the correct port instead of merely identifying a port.
accepted.sec: Guilds → craft, interest rates, Indo-Roman ports  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
accepted.x: Kantakasela was identified with Ghantasala. Maisolia was Machilipatnam, whereas Bharuch and Sopara were separate ports.
accepted.tq: Start from the sure identification of the ancient and modern port names.
accepted.sec: Guilds → craft, interest rates, Indo-Roman ports  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which ancient port is associated with the later Eastern Chalukya period rather than the Satavahana port list?
accepted.x: Motupalli appears as a later Eastern Chalukya-era port. Kantakasela, Maisolia and Koddura occur in the east-coast port context of the Satavahana period.
accepted.tq: Separate the later historical association from the contemporaneous port group.
accepted.sec: Guilds → craft, interest rates, Indo-Roman ports  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Who described the drain of Roman gold and referred to fine cloth in connection with Indian trade?
o: The anonymous author of the Periplus
accepted.x: Pliny, writing in Latin in Natural History, referred to the drain of Roman gold and fine cloth. Ptolemy and the Periplus supplied other commercial references.
accepted.tq: Match the author with both the work and the distinctive commercial observation.
accepted.sec: Guilds → craft, interest rates, Indo-Roman ports  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The Periplus associated Arikamedu with which description?
o: A centre of Roman gold mines
A royal mint of the Satavahanas
A market street of the Romans
accepted.x: The anonymous Greek Periplus described Arikamedu as the “market street of the Romans.”
accepted.tq: Recall the distinctive descriptive phrase linked to the source and site.
accepted.sec: Guilds → craft, interest rates, Indo-Roman ports  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Ptolemy associated which of the following with Masolia and Ben Ra respectively?
o: Textiles and Vengi as a trade centre
Gold mines and a military cantonment
Roman wine and a Buddhist monastery
Iron ore and a royal capital
accepted.x: Ptolemy referred to the textiles of Masolia and identified Ben Ra, corresponding to Vengi, as a trade centre.
accepted.tq: Link two details from the same source before evaluating the options.
accepted.sec: Guilds → craft, interest rates, Indo-Roman ports  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following commodities was imported rather than exported in Satavahana overseas trade?
accepted.x: Camphor from China was an import. Spices, ivory, muslin, pearls and diamonds were listed among exports.
accepted.tq: Separate exports from imports by identifying the direction of movement.
accepted.sec: Guilds → craft, interest rates, Indo-Roman ports  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding Satavahana trade:
1. Wine was imported from Italy and Arabia.
2. Silk and camphor were imported from China.
3. Gold was imported from Malaya and Sumatra.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Wine came from Italy and Arabia, silk and camphor from China, and gold from Malaya and Sumatra. All three statements are correct.
accepted.tq: Check the commodity–source pairs individually before accepting the combined option.
accepted.sec: Guilds → craft, interest rates, Indo-Roman ports  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Foreign traders in the Satavahana period were referred to as:
accepted.x: Sarthavahas were long-distance or foreign traders. Shreshthis were guild heads, while Gahapatis were connected with urban administration.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the trader designation from administrative and guild offices.
accepted.sec: Guilds → craft, interest rates, Indo-Roman ports  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which route correctly represents the inland commercial connection from Ujjain to Bharuch?
accepted.x: The inland route from Ujjain to Bharuch passed through Paithan and Tagara.
accepted.tq: Reconstruct the route by identifying the intermediate inland centres.
accepted.sec: Inland trade routes and centres  [other exams]

accepted.s: Paithan was connected with Sopara through:
accepted.x: The route from Paithan to Sopara passed through Aurangabad.
accepted.tq: Identify the stated intermediate station rather than the endpoint.
accepted.sec: Inland trade routes and centres  [other exams]

accepted.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
accepted.x: Guntupalli was associated with copper and iron, not gold. Guduru, Vinukonda and Palnadu were associated respectively with fine cotton, metal and diamonds.
accepted.tq: Find the changed commodity in an otherwise familiar centre–product list.
accepted.sec: Inland trade routes and centres  [other exams]

accepted.s: Which of the following centres was associated with cloth and ivory?
accepted.x: Vidisha was associated with cloth and ivory. Guduru was known for fine cotton, while Guntupalli was linked with copper and iron.
accepted.tq: Match the centre with its distinctive pair of products.
accepted.sec: Inland trade routes and centres  [other exams]

accepted.s: Iron ore was worked in which of the following areas during the Satavahana period?
accepted.x: Iron ore was worked in the Karimnagar–Warangal area. The other pairs represent trade routes or centres associated with different commodities.
accepted.tq: Use the geographical location rather than the commercial route as the key clue.
accepted.sec: Inland trade routes and centres  [other exams]

accepted.s: Pratishthana, identified with Paithan, was situated on the:
accepted.x: Pratishthana or Paithan was the capital and an inland trade centre situated on the Godavari.
accepted.tq: Link the ancient name, modern identification and river location.
accepted.sec: Inland trade routes and centres  [other exams]

accepted.s: Which of the following statements about Satavahana inland trade is correct?
o: Tagara was an emporium linked to coastal ports.
Vengi was exclusively a military camp.
Pratishthana was only a religious settlement and not a trade centre.
The Satavahanas were known for avoiding the construction of roads.
accepted.x: Tagara was an important emporium linked to coastal ports. Pratishthana was both a capital and inland trade centre, Vengi was a trade centre, and the Satavahanas were famed as road builders.
accepted.tq: Choose the careful functional description and reject reversed or extreme claims.
accepted.sec: Inland trade routes and centres  [other exams]

accepted.s: The Satavahanas were famed as road builders, described by the expression:
accepted.x: Mahapatha nirmatalu means builders or makers of great roads and is associated with the Satavahanas.
accepted.tq: Identify the exact historical expression rather than its general translation alone.
accepted.sec: Inland trade routes and centres  [other exams]

accepted.s: The use of metronymic names such as Gautamiputra among Satavahana rulers primarily indicates:
o: The rejection of all caste distinctions
Respect for mothers within a patriarchal society
The exclusive inheritance of property through women
accepted.x: Metronymics reflected respect for mothers, but Satavahana society remained patriarchal. They do not indicate the complete disappearance of caste or patriarchal institutions.
accepted.tq: Avoid the extreme inference that a matronymic automatically proves a matriarchal society.
accepted.sec: Society - metronymics, caste mobility, women donors, debates  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which statement best reflects the social conditions under the Satavahanas?
o: Chaturvarna operated, while Sakas and Yavanas could be absorbed into society.
Caste mobility was impossible under every circumstance.
The Satavahanas abolished Brahmanical social ideology.
Foreign groups were permanently excluded from the social order.
accepted.x: Chaturvarna operated, and the absorption of Sakas and Yavanas indicates social mobility despite continuing Brahmanical ideology.
accepted.tq: Reconcile the coexistence of social hierarchy and mobility instead of choosing an absolute claim.
accepted.sec: Society - metronymics, caste mobility, women donors, debates  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The claim of being ‘Ekabrahmana’ and of stopping varna-sankara is associated with:
accepted.x: Gautamiputra Satakarni claimed the title or description Ekabrahmana and was associated with stopping varna-sankara, reflecting Brahmanical ideology amid social mobility.
accepted.tq: Match the ideological claim with the correct Satavahana ruler.
accepted.sec: Society - metronymics, caste mobility, women donors, debates  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly describes religious patronage in Satavahana society?
o: Women donors were absent from Buddhist patronage.
Kings and queens exclusively patronised Jainism.
Vedic sacrifices were prohibited by Satavahana rulers.
Kings followed Vedic religion, while queens and women donors patronised Buddhism.
accepted.x: Satavahana kings followed Vedic religion, including the Ashvamedha, while queens and women donors supported Buddhism.
accepted.tq: Compare the religious patronage of rulers with that of queens and women donors.
accepted.sec: Society - metronymics, caste mobility, women donors, debates  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Gautami Balasri is associated with the donation of a:
accepted.x: Gautami Balasri donated a vihara, illustrating the role of women donors in Buddhist patronage.
accepted.tq: Match the donor with the specific religious institution donated.
accepted.sec: Society - metronymics, caste mobility, women donors, debates  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following reflects evidence of maritime activity in the Gathasaptasati and Satavahana coinage?
o: Only land caravans and elephant coins
accepted.x: The Gathasaptasati refers to seafaring merchants, and ship coins provide related evidence of maritime activity.
accepted.tq: Combine the literary and numismatic clues attached to maritime trade.
accepted.sec: Society - metronymics, caste mobility, women donors, debates  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which inscription refers to the Nigama Sabha in the context of Satavahana urban administration?
accepted.x: The Nigama Sabha is referred to in the Bhattiprolu inscription. The Naneghat inscription is also cited in the relevant explanation, but the stated reference here is Bhattiprolu.
accepted.tq: Identify the inscription linked specifically with the urban council reference.
accepted.sec: Urban administration - Nigama Sabha, towns and Gahapati  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which of the following was included among the major Satavahana towns?
accepted.x: Dhanyakataka was among the major Satavahana towns, along with places such as Pratishthana, Vijayapuri, Nasik and Kondapur.
accepted.tq: Select the town from the stated Satavahana urban list rather than from another ancient urban network.
accepted.sec: Urban administration - Nigama Sabha, towns and Gahapati  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which of the following sets contains only towns associated with the Satavahana urban network?
accepted.x: Barukaccha, Sopara, Kalyan and Govardhana are included among the major Satavahana towns. The other sets combine urban centres from different historical contexts.
accepted.tq: Check whether every member belongs to the same stated urban network.
accepted.sec: Urban administration - Nigama Sabha, towns and Gahapati  [APPSC, GROUP-II]
